title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations + kv batching/scheduling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: upgrade our attention execution path to use FlashAttentionV2 variants with fused rotary/rope operations and a KV-cache layout that is friendly to continuous batching and the request-level scheduler. This reduces per-token overhead, lowers memory pressure for long contexts, and enables denser packing in the continuous batcher. Changes: integrated FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fallback to legacy kernels on older CUDA/arch targets; added fused ops for rotary and rope position encodings to avoid extra elementwise kernels; redesigned KV cache memory layout and alignment so that key/value tensors are contiguous per-head and per-layer for faster memcpy and cross-stream reuse; introduced a kernel selection path that chooses fused-rope+flashattnv2 when hardware supports it, otherwise picks the safest compatible kernel. Scheduler/batching: updated continuous_batcher to group inflight requests by compatible kernel profile (seq-len, dtype, rotary vs rope) and pack microbatches to maximize GPU occupancy while respecting latency SLOs. Also added a small heuristics table to prefer fused kernels for long-context requests. Testing: unit tests for kernel selection, kernel fallbacks, and KV layout invariants added; integration perf harness updated with long-context scenarios and kv-cache reuse patterns. CI: initial run failed on a boundary condition in the rotary fusion when head dim % 8 != 0; fixed by adding a scalar fallback path and re-running. Benchmarks: on rtx-a100 equivalent, we see ~30-45% throughput improvement on long-context generation (8k tokens) and ~10-20% mean latency reduction for interactive short generations, with peak memory reduction allowing 1.5x larger effective batch size. No model-quality regressions observed in the eval harness; golden-response diffing and sampling tests passed. Rollout: feature gated and behind a runtime flag; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters for 72h, monitor token-level latency and error-rate dashboards, then full rollout. Rollback: runtime flag and kernel selection fallbacks allow immediate revert to previous kernels without model changes. Related: the change touches attention, kv, scheduler and ops registries; coordinated with infra for canary GPU fleet. See linked Linear tickets for perf goals and canary plan.
